grh_f393d187bca8628a1fbd.title: Girl Trouble
paragraphs: A cold December night brings Dr. Christian into what first looks like an attempted kidnapping. Wealthy schoolboy Johnny is found bound, gagged and nearly frozen on the Ramseysâ€™ porch, and the police assume a gang of boys must be responsible. Dr. Christian is less convinced. He sees that Johnny is under intense pressure from parents who buy him everything but give him little freedom, demand top school performance, control his food and schedule, and leave almost no time for ordinary play. Johnny also has a very obvious adolescent interest in the Ramseysâ€™ pretty daughter Marie. As the boy recovers, Dr. Christian establishes that the crude ropes and wire were no professional kidnapping tools and finally gets to the truth: Johnny staged the incident himself. Rather than punish a frightened and embarrassed boy, the doctor makes his parents recognize how their expectations helped drive him to such a desperate bid for attention. He persuades the police and family to let the matter die quietly, then asks Marie to help Johnny put the episode behind him by refusing to feed further gossip.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on December 5, 1945. It is listed as episode 367 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 23 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_f31474c6c68acc32ff7a.title: The Strange Case of the Iron Box
paragraphs: For generations the Dunbar family has waited to open an iron box of gold on the New Year's Eve before the heir's twenty-first birthday, a delay stretched to eighty-four years because Sir Walter Dunbar was born on February 29. Holmes suspects the box is too light and helps Sir Walter stage a disappearance so the younger Ian Dunbar can force it open. Inside is only an old Murdoch-family IOU proving that the lawyers' ancestor took the gold long ago. Holmes then finds a false bottom containing an unpublished manuscript by Sir Walter Scott, a treasure worth more than the missing sovereigns and enough to rescue the family's hopes.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.0840817a7be61c6f|Silver Blaze]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_f345fb22bed2cd1bc7df.title: The Purloined Ruby
paragraphs: An actress is watched by a man whose family has spent generations seeking a legendary giant ruby, and Holmes becomes involved when her jewel disappears. The chase leads to a darkened theater where the recovered ruby is planted as bait and Holmes is fired upon from hiding. grh_f35c7766115deb1d19b6.title: The Disappearing Scientists
paragraphs: On the eve of Holmes's retirement to Sussex, the three assistants of radium researcher Professor Buller disappear one after another, followed by Buller himself and the university's precious radium. Buller is found murdered and the three assistants soon return with convenient explanations, leaving Holmes apparently without a clue. The wound, however, proves the killer was right-handed. Holmes recalls Buller's joking description of assistant Jeffrey Barker as 'adroit' while Taylor and Gladys Hughes were 'gauche': literally, right and left. Only Barker could have made the fatal thrust. A telegram confirms the arrest and recovery of the radium.
